Recorded. Fifth and final question.

**Question:** When a bookmark's tags differ in capitalisation — say `Python`, `cli`, and `API` — what counts as "alphabetical order" for the tags column? (FR-014, FR-018, FR-020)

**Why it matters:** Sorting raw text puts every capitalised tag ahead of every lowercase one (`API, Python, cli`), which looks wrong to a user expecting `API, cli, Python` — and FR-014's tests have to assert one exact order.

**Recommended:** Option A — sort while ignoring capitalisation, displaying each tag with the capitalisation it was stored in, and fall back to the raw text when two tags differ only by case so the order is always the same for the same input. This matches what "alphabetical" means to a reader and stays a single sort expression.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | Case-insensitive alphabetical, original capitalisation preserved in output, raw text as tie-breaker |
| B | Raw character-code order, so all capitalised tags sort before lowercase ones |
| C | Normalise tags to lowercase when storing, making the question moot (changes FR-010) |
| Short | Provide a different short answer (<=5 words) |

You can reply with the option letter (e.g., "A"), accept the recommendation by saying "yes" or "recommended", or provide your own short answer.
